_about: How the teacher sounds to a child in English: the one place to edit her words. DRAFT written by Claude and not yet checked by a Nigerian teacher; replace any line. Every line must pass the tutor's line rules (two sentences at most, ten words or fewer each, no digits, no grown-up words). {number} is the number the child said, in words; {Number} starts a sentence.
right_with_you: Good, you said it with me.
That is it. Now you try it on your own.
Yes, with me. Now by yourself.

when they almost had it: Almost! Listen, then say it: one, two, three, four, five.
Nearly there. Listen again, then you try.
when a list broke part of the way: You got as far as fifty-five.
Good, you counted up to Thursday.
when they got it wrong: Not yet. Listen, then say it: five, ten, fifteen.
Listen: seven times three is twenty-one. Say it after me.
when they said they do not know: No problem. Say it after me: one, two, three.
It is fine, we start small. Say five.
when the phone did not hear them: I did not hear you. Say it again, a little louder.
